texts.text: Weather Report

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · A large system brought significant rains to much of the Southwest region and parts of the Interlake. Scattered rains were observed throughout the Northwest and Central regions. The largest accumulations occurred in the Southwest with Reston receiving 111 mm of rain over August 14 and 15.
texts.text: A large system brought significant rains to much of the Southwest region and parts of the Interlake. Scattered rains were observed throughout the Northwest and Central regions. The largest accumulations occurred in the Southwest with Reston receiving 111 mm of rain over August 14 and 15.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Climate normals for total accumulated precipitation from May 1 to August 16 range from 202 mm to 307 mm and are based on 30-year historical data. Since May 1, areas of the Northwest, Southwest, and Interlake regions have accumulated more than 300 mm of precipitation. Seasonal accumulations are above normal for the majority of the Northwest and Southwest regions. The southern Interlake in the Stonewall, Petersfield, and Woodlands areas have seen accumulations over 150% of normal. A few localized areas of the Interlake, Central and Eastern regions have seen accumulations below 80% of the 30-year average.

texts.orig: · Total Accumulation of Growing Degree Days shows the accumulated growing degree days (GDD) for the period of May 1 - August 16, 2026. GDD accumulations ranged between 1036 and 1442 GDD so far, this growing season. Most of southern Manitoba has accumulated more than 1250 GDD.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Recent rainfall over the weekend improved pasture conditions, replenished dugouts and encouraged forage regrowth after hot, and in some areas, dry conditions. The improved conditions allowed producers to move cattle to areas with better grass, where forage supplies had become limited.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Southwest
texts.text: Southwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Harvest began in some areas of the Southwest early last week, but rainfall in the middle of the week brought all fieldwork to a stop. Most areas reported rainfall amounts of 50 to 100 mm. Much of this moisture was beneficial for late season crops such as corn and soybeans, given the extended dry spell. Conditions are beginning to dry, but several areas of fields still have standing water, along with significant crop lodging. Local creeks and rivers are returning to normal flows.

Conditions are beginning to dry, but several areas of fields still have standing water, along with significant crop lodging. Local creeks and rivers are returning to normal flows.
